research_question: How much of eGSK's panel standing depends on the SciPy-SLSQP substitution for the published MATLAB fmincon SQP polish?
current_evidence_gap: The substitution is disclosed but bounded only for runtime/environment (performance.tex:32-39; supplementary.tex:1766-1773). Read-only instrumentation of the shipped port shows the substituted solver consumes 0-16.6% of MaxFES at D=10 and 0-11.0% at D=30 (16,600/100,000 on F26 D10; 33,100/300,000 on F26 D30), so it is load-bearing on exactly the class the paper analyses by name. eGSK is the only comparator that outranks DT-GSK anywhere (CEC2017 D30 2.29 vs 2.50; CEC2011 2.52 vs 3.36, p_Holm=4.2e-2) and the two are never Nemenyi-separable. No admissible evidence bounds the sign or size of the solver effect.
minimum_design: Three-arm eGSK contrast on CEC2017 D=30 only, 29 functions x 51 runs, identical seed schedule, budget and evaluator: (A) shipped SLSQP port; (B) polish disabled (_egsk_ip_refine returns immediately, budget left to the main loop); (C) a second bounded local solver at the same per-call evaluation budget (e.g. scipy L-BFGS-B or Powell) as a solver-swap control. 3 x 1,479 = 4,437 runs; ~3-5 h at the measured eGSK per-run cost.
controls: Same 51-seed schedule, same shared X0, same MaxFES=300,000, same evaluator build, same host and worker count; only the polish backend varies. All three arms produced in one session at one commit to avoid the S8-04 cross-commit issue.
scope: CEC2017 D=30 (the dimension where eGSK leads DT-GSK). Extend to CEC2011 only if arm B moves the D=30 ordering.
endpoint: Per-function mean error over 51 runs; Friedman mean rank of eGSK within the fixed 7-panel recomputed with each arm substituted for the shipped eGSK column.
analysis: Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank over the 29 per-function means, arm A vs B and A vs C, with matched-pairs rank-biserial effect size; report the induced change in the panel Friedman mean rank and in the DT-GSK vs eGSK Holm decision.
expected_decision_impact: If |rank shift| < ~0.15 and the DT-GSK vs eGSK Holm decisions are unchanged, the solver substitution is bounded as immaterial and the class-B qualification can be stated with a number. If the shift is larger, the DT-GSK vs eGSK cells must be reported as solver-sensitive and the non-separability statement re-qualified.
admissible_evidence_available: No. Nothing in rel-2026-07-20-67d9345f9 varies the eGSK polish backend; the ablation release covers DT-GSK components only.
claim_affected: LM-04 (eGSK provenance/comparability); the CEC2017 D30 second place; the CEC2011 Holm-significant loss; the DT-GSK/eGSK non-separability statement
estimated_scientific_value: High - it is the single measurement that converts the paper's most likely reviewer objection from unanswerable to bounded, at a few hours of compute.

research_question: Do AGSK, APGSK and FDB-AGSK change the panel standings when run at the dimension-scaled initial populations their own publications specify, rather than at the normalised NP_init=100 used here?
current_evidence_gap: mohamed2020agsk p.3 specifies NP=20*D, apgsk2021 p.4 specifies 200*D, fdbagsk2023 p.10 Eq.(62) specifies 40*n; all three were run at a flat NP_init=100 (run_experiment.py:284-290; agsk.py:209-210; apgsk.py:73-74; fdb_agsk.py:204-205) while DT-GSK runs 5*D. The normalisation has published precedent (jawad2024egsk Tab.3) but the manuscript asserts the constants are the cited papers' constants and discloses no deviation, so the effect on the standings is unbounded and undisclosed.
minimum_design: Two-cell sensitivity at the extremes of the grid: re-run AGSK, APGSK and FDB-AGSK at CEC2017 D=10 and D=100, 29 functions x 51 runs, with NP_init set to each algorithm's published rule (AGSK 20*D; FDB-AGSK 40*D; APGSK 200*D at D=10 and a stated, justified transposition at D=100 - e.g. min(200*D, MaxFES/50) - with the transposition rule declared in the paper). 3 algorithms x 2 dims x 1,479 = 8,874 runs; the other four panel columns are reused unchanged from the release.
controls: Identical seed schedule, shared X0 regenerated at the new NP, identical MaxFES and evaluator, same host/workers, single commit. NP_min held at 12 for all arms. Only NP_init varies.
scope: CEC2017 D=10 and D=100. D=30/50 and the other suites only if either extreme reverses an ordering.
endpoint: Per-function mean error over 51 runs; recomputed 7-panel Friedman mean ranks at D=10 and D=100; DT-GSK vs each of the three comparators, Wilcoxon + Holm (family 6).
analysis: Recompute the per-dimension Friedman ranks and the Holm-corrected pairwise decisions with the re-populated comparator columns; report as a preregistered robustness variant alongside the frozen primary, never replacing it.
expected_decision_impact: If DT-GSK's ordinal position (1st at D=10 and D=100) and the sign of every Holm decision are unchanged, the normalisation is bounded as immaterial and the S8-02 disclosure can cite it. If any ordinal or sign flips, the affected rank claims must be qualified as configuration-sensitive.
admissible_evidence_available: No. Every released comparator cell uses NP_init=100; no alternative-NP cell exists anywhere in the release or the ablation tree.
claim_affected: T-PANEL 'published reference constants' rows; RS-01 (CEC2017 overall rank); the D=10 and D=100 first places; comparability_audit.md 'Transparent parameter-tuning effort' PASS
estimated_scientific_value: High - it is the only evidence that would let the paper keep a strong fairness statement about the three LPSR comparators instead of a bare declared deviation.

research_question: Does the AGSK/APGSK target-error early-stop rule, which the other five optimizers do not implement, move any reported statistic?
current_evidence_gap: 1,845 of 41,412 CEC2017+CEC2013 panel runs terminate below MaxFES, all of them AGSK or APGSK (agsk.py:348-355; apgsk.py:234). The neutrality argument is analytic (stop threshold 1e-8 equals the reporting floor; error forced to 0; all 400 AGSK/APGSK checkpoint logs verified complete with 0 ragged rows and 0 blank cells) but has never been checked numerically against the frozen tables.
minimum_design: Analysis-only; no new runs. Recompute the affected panels from the existing release under two variants: (i) treat every early-stopped run's endpoint as its recorded value (the frozen basis) and (ii) as the un-floored value at the checkpoint immediately preceding the stop; and separately recompute the D=10 and D=30 panels with the early-stopped runs excluded from the affected functions. Report the maximum absolute change in any Friedman mean rank and any Holm decision.
controls: Same release, same analysis code path (papers/scripts/phase6_run_analysis.py), same seeds; only the endpoint-treatment rule varies.
scope: CEC2017 D=10, D=30 and CEC2013 D=10, D=30 - the only cells containing early stops.
endpoint: Friedman mean rank per dimension; Holm decision per (comparator, dimension) cell.
analysis: Deterministic recomputation; report max |delta rank| and any decision flip. Present as a robustness row, not a new primary.
expected_decision_impact: Expected to confirm zero change (the analytic argument is strong). Its value is that it converts the S8-01 disclosure from an argument into a check, which is what §5.4 requires to close a ticket.
admissible_evidence_available: Yes - partially. The release contains everything needed; the recomputation has simply never been run. No new evidence release is required because nothing is promoted.
claim_affected: PR-04 (budgets); the corrected budget-equality sentence at performance.tex:169-170
estimated_scientific_value: Moderate - low cost, closes S8-01 with a check rather than an assurance, per §5.4.

research_question: How large is the optimistic-selection bias in the CEC2017 headline rank, given that the frozen configuration was selected on CEC2017 against the same panel and the same statistic?
current_evidence_gap: supplementary.tex:1157-1161 discloses that 'several full-panel candidate configurations were compared against the family panel' without stating how many, on which cells, or under which selection statistic, and the candidates are outside the immutable release. The multiplicity of the selection stage is therefore unbounded, while the confirmatory analysis controls multiplicity only within each dimension family.
minimum_design: Two tiers. Tier 1 (disclosure, no compute, submission-blocking): author attestation of the candidate count k, the cells scored, and the selection statistic - or an explicit statement that k was not logged. Tier 2 (empirical, optional): re-score the k retained candidate configurations on CEC2011 and CEC2013 only (both held out of selection) and report the promoted configuration's held-out rank against the alternatives; if the candidates were not archived, report instead the promoted configuration's held-out standing as the sole unbiased estimate and label the CEC2017 rank as selected.
controls: Held-out suites only for the unbiased estimate; identical protocol, seeds and budgets to the primary campaign.
endpoint: Tier 1: k, selection cells, selection statistic. Tier 2: held-out Friedman mean rank of each candidate.
analysis: Tier 1 is descriptive disclosure. Tier 2: compare the promoted configuration's held-out rank to the candidate distribution; the gap between selected (CEC2017) and held-out (CEC2011/CEC2013) standing is the informal optimism estimate.
expected_decision_impact: Tier 1 makes the exposure auditable and is required regardless of outcome. Tier 2 would let the paper state the optimism bound rather than gesture at it. Neither changes a frozen number.
admissible_evidence_available: No for Tier 2 - the intermediate candidates are explicitly not part of the immutable evidence release. Yes for Tier 1 - it is an author attestation, requiring no evidence release.
claim_affected: R6-T03 (selection-exposure disclosure); RS-01 (CEC2017 overall rank 2.48); the abstract's 'CEC2017 was configuration-selection exposed' sentence
estimated_scientific_value: High for Tier 1 at zero cost - a quantified exposure is defensible, a vague one invites the reviewer to assume the worst. Moderate for Tier 2.

research_question: Does DT-GSK's self-initialisation - the one documented departure from the shared X0 protocol - account for any part of its measured advantage?
current_evidence_gap: DT-GSK draws its own 5*D initial population and does not consume the runner's shared X0 (dt_gsk.py:14-18), disclosed at performance.tex:117-124 and flagged in the limitations as 'a disclosed fairness asymmetry that is not separately bounded'. No reported inference depends on run-level pairing (the inferential unit is the function; run-level A12 is unpaired; BCa resamples fixed per-function midranks), so the asymmetry cannot invalidate a test - but its performance contribution has never been measured.
minimum_design: Initialisation-swap control on CEC2017 D=10 and D=30 (the tiers where the limitation says the asymmetry matters most), 29 functions x 51 runs: run DT-GSK unchanged except that its initial population's first min(5*D, 100) rows are taken from the runner's shared X0 for that (dim, func, run) and the remainder drawn from its own stream. 2 x 1,479 = 2,958 runs. Requires a controlled deviation build, not a change to the byte-locked shipped optimizer, and must be reported as a control arm outside the frozen release.
controls: Identical seeds, budget, evaluator, host and frozen profile; only the source of the initial rows varies. Comparator columns reused unchanged.
endpoint: Per-function mean error over 51 runs; DT-GSK's Friedman mean rank in the fixed 7-panel at each dimension.
analysis: Paired Wilcoxon over 29 per-function means, shipped self-init vs shared-start arm, with rank-biserial effect size; report the induced change in DT-GSK's mean rank and in its Holm decisions.
expected_decision_impact: If the shared-start arm is statistically indistinguishable, the asymmetry is bounded as immaterial and the limitation can be closed with a number. If it is not, the low-dimension standings need an initialisation qualification.
admissible_evidence_available: No. Every released DT-GSK cell uses self-init; no shared-start DT-GSK cell exists.
claim_affected: PR-06 (fair-start exception); LM-03; the D=10 and D=30 standings
estimated_scientific_value: Moderate - closes a self-declared unbounded asymmetry, but the design already prevents it from affecting any test, so the value is presentational rather than inferential.

research_question: Where does the GSK family - and DT-GSK within it - stand against strong non-GSK baselines (L-SHADE-class, CMA-ES, differential-grouping decomposition) under the identical locked protocol?
current_evidence_gap: No external baseline is evaluated; the standings are interpretable only inside the seven-algorithm panel, which the paper states plainly (supplementary.tex 'Limitations in Full', seventh item) and bounds with NFL (performance.tex:871-875). Five of the six comparators were authored or co-authored by two of the present authors, which the paper also discloses.
minimum_design: OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS CYCLE - recorded for register completeness only, with no ticket and no gate consequence. Were it in scope: 2-3 external baselines at published settings on CEC2017 all four dimensions, 29 functions x 51 runs, identical seeds/budget/evaluator, added as extra columns to the existing panel.
controls: Identical seed schedule, budget, evaluator, host; baselines at their own published constants with any transposition declared.
endpoint: Per-function mean error; Friedman mean rank in the extended panel.
analysis: Friedman + Iman-Davenport on the extended panel; Wilcoxon + Holm within each dimension family.
expected_decision_impact: Would convert every panel-scoped statement into a field-calibrated one. Not required for any claim the paper currently makes, all of which are explicitly panel-bounded per §10.5.
admissible_evidence_available: No - and explicitly not required. PAPER_REVIEW_PROMPT.md §1.5.4 rules external non-GSK baselines out of scope for this cycle and forbids treating them as a missing requirement, fairness gap, or rejection risk; this seat raises no ticket on this axis.
claim_affected: none - every comparative claim is already bounded to the GSK-family panel
estimated_scientific_value: High in absolute terms, but out of scope by governing directive for this submission cycle; the paper already names it as future work.

research_question: Are the six comparator cells re-derivable under a pinned environment, and how large is the drift that made the 2026-07-21 re-execution fail?
current_evidence_gap: RT-001 records that re-running the six comparators at a later commit produced 3,772 scientific-column diffs, worst for atmals-gsk (~31%) and egsk (~29%), attributed to version/floating-point drift amplified by chaotic search. The panel itself was produced across seven producer commits over ten days (environment.json git_commit per cell). No manuscript surface discloses either fact, and no measurement isolates whether the drift is library-version or code-change induced.
minimum_design: Analysis-plus-narrow-rerun. (i) Diff the six comparator source files between each cell's producer commit and the current HEAD to establish whether any comparator code changed at all. (ii) Re-run one small cell per comparator (one function x 5 seeds x one dimension) at the original producer commit inside a pinned dependency environment reconstructed from pyproject.toml, and compare against the released rows bit-for-bit. 6 x 5 = 30 runs.
controls: Same seeds, same evaluator data, same host; the only varying factor between the two arms is the interpreter/dependency stack.
scope: One representative CEC2017 cell per comparator (suggest F12 D=30).
endpoint: Bit-level identity of best_fitness / error / nfes against the released rows.
analysis: Report per-comparator identity rate and, where identity fails, the magnitude of the first divergence and the generation at which it appears.
expected_decision_impact: If identity is recovered under a pinned stack, the release is reproducible-with-pinning and the S8-04 limitation can say so precisely, which is a materially stronger statement than 'not re-derivable'. If identity is not recovered even under pinning, the limitation must stand as written.
admissible_evidence_available: No. The release records producer commits and probe hashes but contains no cross-environment re-derivation cell.
claim_affected: LM-03 ('one code base, one protocol and one harness'); CN-02 (re-derivability); the sixth limitation (single host/environment)
estimated_scientific_value: Moderate-to-high - it would convert an unqualified reproducibility gap into a bounded, pinned-environment guarantee, at ~30 runs of compute.
